Name: Black-capped Chickadee
Fun fact: Maine's state bird. Hides thousands of seeds each fall and remembers where they are.

Name: Blue Jay
Fun fact: Can imitate the scream of a Red-tailed Hawk.

Name: American Crow
Fun fact: Crows recognize individual human faces and remember them for years.

Name: Northern Cardinal
Fun fact: Only arrived in Maine in the mid-1900s, following backyard feeders north.

Name: Tufted Titmouse
Fun fact: Plucks hair from sleeping animals to line its nest.

Name: White-breasted Nuthatch
Fun fact: Walks headfirst down tree trunks, spotting insects other birds miss.

Name: Red-breasted Nuthatch
Fun fact: Smears sticky pine pitch around its nest hole to keep intruders out.

Name: Downy Woodpecker
Fun fact: North America's smallest woodpecker.

Name: Hairy Woodpecker
Fun fact: Looks like a Downy but with a beak almost as long as its head.

Name: Pileated Woodpecker
Fun fact: Crow-sized, and leaves rectangular holes big enough to fit your hand.

Name: American Goldfinch
Fun fact: Turns from drab olive in winter to bright yellow each spring.

Name: Mourning Dove
Fun fact: Its wings whistle on takeoff, a built-in alarm for the flock.

Name: European Starling
Fun fact: All North American starlings descend from about 100 birds released in New York in 1890.

Name: Rock Pigeon
Fun fact: Can find its way home from hundreds of miles away.

Name: Dark-eyed Junco
Fun fact: Called the 'snowbird' because flocks show up as winter arrives.

Name: American Robin
Fun fact: Hunts worms by sight. Rain brings them to the surface, and robins to your lawn.

Name: Song Sparrow
Fun fact: Each male sings up to 20 different song patterns.

Name: Cedar Waxwing
Fun fact: Sometimes gets tipsy from eating fermented berries.

Name: Bald Eagle
Fun fact: Maine has more nesting pairs than any other northeastern state.

Name: Red-tailed Hawk
Fun fact: Its scream is the 'eagle sound' used in most movies.

Name: Osprey
Fun fact: Dives feet-first into the water to catch fish.

Name: Great Horned Owl
Fun fact: Nests in January, often while snow covers the eggs.

Name: Barred Owl
Fun fact: Calls 'Who cooks for you? Who cooks for you-all?'

Name: Snowy Owl
Fun fact: Arctic visitor that hunts in daylight and turns up on beaches and airfields.

Name: Red-winged Blackbird
Fun fact: Males flash red shoulder patches to claim cattail territory.

Name: Common Yellowthroat
Fun fact: Wears a black bandit mask and sings 'witchety-witchety'.

Name: Yellow Warbler
Fun fact: Buries cowbird eggs laid in its nest under a new nest floor.

Name: Black-throated Green Warbler
Fun fact: Sings a buzzy 'zee-zee-zoo-zee' from the tops of pines and hemlocks.

Name: Red-eyed Vireo
Fun fact: Can sing more than 20,000 songs in a single day.

Name: Gray Catbird
Fun fact: Its call sounds just like a meowing cat.

Name: Ruby-throated Hummingbird
Fun fact: Weighs less than a nickel and flies non-stop across the Gulf of Mexico.

Name: Tree Swallow
Fun fact: Catches insects in mid-air, swooping low over water.

Name: Great Blue Heron
Fun fact: Stands motionless for minutes, then spears fish faster than you can blink.

Name: Double-crested Cormorant
Fun fact: Spreads its wings to dry them because its feathers aren't fully waterproof.

Name: Eastern Phoebe
Fun fact: Says its own name: 'fee-bee!' and loves nesting under porches and bridges.

Name: Bobolink
Fun fact: Migrates about 12,000 miles round trip to Argentina each year.

Name: American Woodcock
Fun fact: Its spring 'sky dance' at dusk spirals hundreds of feet up, then tumbles back down.

Name: Killdeer
Fun fact: Fakes a broken wing to lead predators away from its nest.

Name: Baltimore Oriole
Fun fact: Weaves a hanging sock-shaped nest at the tip of a branch.

Name: Scarlet Tanager
Fun fact: Brilliant red, yet hard to spot in the high forest canopy.

Name: Herring Gull
Fun fact: Will drop clams on rocks and parking lots to crack them open.

Name: Great Black-backed Gull
Fun fact: The largest gull in the world.

Name: Common Eider
Fun fact: Its down feathers are among the warmest natural insulation on Earth.

Name: Mallard
Fun fact: Nearly every domestic duck breed descends from the Mallard.

Name: American Black Duck
Fun fact: Winters along Maine's salt marshes in large rafts.

Name: Common Loon
Fun fact: Its haunting wail carries for miles across lakes on summer nights.

Name: Snow Bunting
Fun fact: Arctic breeder that roams winter beaches and fields in swirling flocks.

Name: Bufflehead
Fun fact: Small enough to nest in old Northern Flicker holes.

Name: Long-tailed Duck
Fun fact: Dives over 200 feet deep, one of the deepest-diving ducks.

Name: Common Goldeneye
Fun fact: Its wings whistle so loudly it's nicknamed the 'whistler'.

Name: Purple Sandpiper
Fun fact: Spends winter on wave-battered rocks where few other birds can stand.

Name: Pine Siskin
Fun fact: Shows up in big numbers some winters and is almost absent in others.

Name: Evening Grosbeak
Fun fact: A loud, chunky finch whose winter visits are unpredictable.

Name: Semipalmated Sandpiper
Fun fact: Fattens up on Maine mudflats before flying non-stop to South America.

Name: Black-bellied Plover
Fun fact: Often the first to sound the alarm on a mudflat, warning the whole flock.
